roleTitle: Capacity Planning Analyst, Enterprise Knowledge Base
jobDescription: The enterprise knowledge base product serves search and document sync to field staff at large customers. The Capacity Planning Analyst forecasts search and sync load per customer, plans index and storage capacity with the platform team, and is expected to reduce capacity-related incidents, reported against the platform's published incident baseline.
requirements: Keeps a per-customer forecast of search and sync load and the model behind it.
Turns the forecast into index and storage plans agreed with the platform team.
Reduces capacity-related incidents, reported against the published incident baseline.
Takes capacity changes through the platform and customer teams and records who approved what.
Keeps an assumptions note per planning cycle with limitations and hand-over items.

evidence.text: Kept the per-customer load model that predicts search queries and sync volume from user counts and document growth; every month I recalibrated it against the platform metrics warehouse.
Turned each quarter's forecast into an index-shard and storage plan that the platform team and I took to the quarterly planning meeting.

Capacity-related incidents fell from 7 in the first half of the year to 2 in the second half after the shard rebalancing plan was applied, as counted in the platform incident register against its published baseline of 7 incidents per half-year.

Took capacity changes through the quarterly planning meeting with the platform and customer teams; the platform lead approved shard changes and the customer teams handled communication with their accounts.
Kept an assumptions note per cycle covering the model inputs, the fact that bulk document imports sat outside the forecast, and what the next cycle inherited.

Work sample: a year of the incident register filtered to capacity-related incidents (with the baseline and the rebalancing plan marked) and one cycle's assumptions note; export identifiers are included for tracing.
Reference call with the former platform lead: the incident counts are from the platform incident register, the shard rebalancing plan was the candidate's proposal, and the employment dates match.
Recruiter logistics note: prefers to start next quarter; can join a planning workshop on site before then.

propositions.text: The candidate maintained the per-customer load model for search and sync and recalibrated it monthly from the metrics warehouse.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the load model directly.

propositions.text: The candidate planned index shards and storage headroom each quarter with the platform team from the forecast.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the capacity planning work.

propositions.text: Capacity-related incidents fell from 7 to 2 per half-year after the shard rebalancing plan, as counted in the incident register against a baseline of 7.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the counts, the period, the baseline and the register; the work sample and the reference confirm them.

gold.expectedGap: Hand-over conditions for each planning cycle are only partly documented in the assumptions notes.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the incident result as stated for the two half-years; do not extend it to other incident categories.
followUpTargets: Ask how hand-over items were recorded at the end of each planning cycle.
